bindings.label: Asymptomatic nodule on scalp for 3 months
Patient is a man in his 40s with no systemic complaints, no history of arthropod bite, immunosuppression, travel abroad, or contact with animals in the recent past

Physical examination revealed a skin-colored, firm, nontender, freely mobile 2 × 1.5-cm nodule with overlying normal skin on the right occipital region of the scalp; there was no lymphadenopathy and no other cutaneous lesions
Histopathology shows parasite cross-sections with cuticular ridges, outer cuticle, muscle layer, and gravid uterus containing microfilariae, surrounded by fibrous capsule and mixed inflammation
The scalp nodule is a parasitic infection (e.g., filarial nodule)
Peripheral blood smear was negative for microfilariae
Serological testing for filariasis was not performed (unavailable)
Ultrasound examination of the nodule was not performed (unavailable)
The scalp nodule is an occult filarial infection (microfilariae present in tissue but absent from peripheral blood)
